The strongest ground is that the promise was oral, since many states require a signed writing from the debtor to revive a debt already barred by the statute of limitations. The bar alone does not make the promise unenforceable, because Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 82 treats a promise to pay a barred debt as binding without new consideration. The "deadbeat" remark is a distractor that supplies no duress or consideration.

CONFIDENCE: 60
